fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Persona Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey, its logic, and the database behind it from one prompt, then changes any part when you ask.
fields.feature_1:
Questions aimed at your personas

Name the groups you think exist and what sets each one apart. Emergent writes questions that can separate those groups, and a second prompt rewords one or adds a choice.
fields.feature_2:
One row per respondent, yours

Each finished survey becomes a row in a database you own, one answer per column. Next year's rows land beside this year's, so a persona that grew shows in the count.
fields.feature_3:
Follow-up questions for one group only

Ask Emergent to show extra questions only to people who give a certain answer. A student who plans to sell sees questions on where they sell; a hobbyist skips to the end.
fields.feature_4:
A persona label on every respondent

Describe a rule in plain words, such as a donor who first came to volunteer, and the app labels each matching row. The dashboard keeps a running count for every persona.
fields.feature_5:
Labels that travel to your CRM

Connect HubSpot or any CRM with an API, and the app writes each respondent's persona label onto their contact record. Sales can filter by persona without the survey open.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code

Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits, so the survey link can match your brand. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and build on it.
fields.why_description: Surveys built with Emergent have no response caps. Send the persona survey to every customer, and every reply counts toward a persona.

fields.usecase_heading: Persona Surveys That Changed a Plan
fields.tab_content_1:
Who buys payroll? Office managers, 188 of 412

Plumbline Payroll asks 412 customers for their role and head count. The app gives the office manager persona to anyone in that role at a firm under 20 staff, and the count comes to 188. Finance leads make up 141 and outside bookkeepers 83. The homepage now speaks to the office manager.
fields.tab_content_2:
Planning on Sunday, shopping in pairs

Skillethouse asks 960 users of its meal-planning app when they plan the week's meals. Sunday wins with 402, ahead of 351 who decide the night of and 207 who plan around a diet. A follow-up finds 288 of the 402 Sunday planners shop with a partner. A shared shopping list moves into the next release.
fields.tab_content_3:
231 donors came from an adoption

Every donor on the Hollyburn Animal Rescue list gets one question: what first led you to give? Adopting a pet there leads with 231 of 538 answers. Volunteering accounts for 164 and a social post for 143. The monthly giving appeal now goes to adopters first, timed to the anniversary of each adoption.
fields.tab_content_4:
Pricing help for 96 students who sell

Glazeworks Studio asks students why they take ceramics classes. Of 366 students, 96 plan to sell their work and 270 throw for fun. Only students who plan to sell see the next questions, on where they sell: 58 at craft markets and 38 through an online shop. The studio adds a spring class on pricing handmade pieces.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Persona Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write persona survey questions that split respondents into clear groups, then build and test the survey with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about the last real time
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what the personas are for before you draft a question: a homepage rewrite, say, or which donors get an appeal first. Any question that cannot change that choice comes out.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down the two to four personas you expect and one trait that would prove each one. Those traits become your sorting questions, such as job role or the reason someone first gave.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask what people did, not what they might do. A question about the last week they planned meals describes a real week; a question about how often they plan invites a guess.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Use multiple choice for any question that places someone in a persona, with one answer per group. Save open text for a single question about what made them start looking.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask for age or location only when a persona depends on it. Place those questions at the end of the survey, after the ones about the respondent's own habits.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Build it and test the labels
fields.howto_step_6_des: Paste your questions and persona rules into one prompt, and Emergent builds the survey with its labels and dashboard. Take it yourself five times as five different people and check where each lands.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Call a few people per persona
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once the counts settle, call three people from each persona and ask them to walk you through their last purchase or donation. Their stories explain the why behind each count.

faq_plan.a: Persona survey questions are the questions that sort the people who answer into a small set of groups, or personas, by traits such as their job or what made them start looking. A useful set pairs a few closed sorting questions with one open question about motivation, and the answers give you a count for each persona.

faq_plan.q: How do I create persona survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Write one multiple-choice question for each trait that separates the groups you already suspect, with one answer choice per group. Describe those personas in plain English to Emergent's AI survey builder, and it builds the survey along with a dashboard that counts each persona.

faq_plan.q: How many people should answer persona survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Aim for enough that your smallest persona has a few dozen answers of its own; the size of each group matters more than the total. If one persona ends up with a handful of rows, send the survey to more people like them before acting on its count. Emergent sets no response caps on the survey, and the whole list can answer.

faq_plan.q: Should persona survey questions be open-ended or multiple choice?
faq_plan.a: Use both. Multiple choice works for the questions that place someone in a persona, because each answer maps to one group. One or two open questions on motivation give you the words each persona uses, which help when you later write copy for them.

faq_plan.q: How do buyer persona survey questions differ from user persona survey questions?
faq_plan.a: A buyer persona survey asks the people who choose and pay for a product about their role and what started their search. A user persona survey asks the people who use it day to day about their tasks and habits. In a business purchase those can be different people, and each survey should go to the right contacts.

faq_plan.q: Should persona survey questions include demographics?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if a persona turns on them, and no otherwise. Ask for age, income, or location if it changes what you will do for that group; otherwise the question lengthens the survey without telling the groups apart. When you do ask, offer a prefer-not-to-say choice on each one.

faq_plan.q: Who should answer persona survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Send it to current customers first, because their answers describe people who already chose you. Add recent prospects who did not buy if you want to see a persona you are losing, and give each list its own link. The answers land in a database you own, with each list's rows kept apart.

faq_plan.q: How many persona survey questions should one survey have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to 10 questions or fewer. Cut any question whose answer would not move someone into a different persona or change what you do for one. Surveys built with Emergent can show one question per screen, which suits respondents taking it on a phone.

faq_plan.q: Can persona survey questions replace customer interviews?
faq_plan.a: No. The survey tells you how many people sit in each persona, and a short interview with a few people from each one tells you why they act as they do. Pick interviewees from the survey results, where each respondent already carries a persona label.

faq_plan.q: How do I turn answers to persona survey questions into personas?
faq_plan.a: Group the respondents by their answers to the sorting questions, count each group, and name it after the trait that sets it apart. Merge any group too small to act on into its nearest neighbor. Then read the open answers inside each group for the words and reasons that belong in its persona profile.

plan.angle: The live SERP is buyer persona question lists (42, 100, 150 questions) and two survey-tool guides; none shows which answers split respondents into personas or what a team changed once the personas existed. This page treats persona survey questions as the few questions that sort real customers, users, donors or students into groups, and shows four surveys built from a prompt that each end in a count per persona and one decision. The how-to gives question-writing practice as plain advice, and the FAQ covers sample size, question types, buyer versus user personas, demographics, who to ask, length, interviews and incentives with no third-party claims.
tab_stories: Plumbline Payroll asks 412 customers about their role and company size; 188 are office managers at firms under 20 staff, 141 finance leads at firms of 20 to 100, and 83 outside bookkeepers, and the homepage is rewritten for the office manager.

Skillethouse, a meal-planning app, asks 960 users when they plan the week's meals; 402 plan on Sunday, 351 decide the night of, and 207 plan around a diet, and 288 of the 402 Sunday planners shop with a partner, so a shared shopping list moves into the next release.

Hollyburn Animal Rescue asks 538 donors what first led them to give; 231 adopted a pet there, 164 volunteered, and 143 found the rescue through a social post, and the monthly giving appeal goes to adopters first.

Glazeworks Studio asks 366 students why they take ceramics classes; 270 throw for fun and 96 plan to sell, and only those 96 see follow-up questions on where they sell (58 at craft markets, 38 in an online shop), so the studio adds a pricing class for sellers.
